newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: African Devt Bank sees 60 pct rise in net income.
newsitem.headline: African Devt Bank sees 60 pct rise in net income.

text.p: The African Development Bank (AfDB) on Monday forecast a rise of about 60 percent in its net income for 1997, following a 50 percent rise in 1996 compared to 1995.

In a presentation ahead of its annual meeting which begins on Wednesday, AfDB officials forecast net income of 163.6 million units of account for 1997 against 103.6 million in 1996 and 69.0 million in 1995.
One AfDB unit of account was worth $1.4380 as at December 31, 1996.
Bank officials attributed the improvement to a fall in the number of non-performing loans thanks to more rigorous lending policies, plus a reduction in running costs.
The AfDB has gone through a period of restructuring following criticism of its management by shareholders, led by Western donor nations.
Donors refused to replenish the Bank's soft loan arm, the African Development Fund (ADF), until changes were made, effectively closing the Fund for two years until May 1996.
One important change has been to limit access to Bank funds to 13 creditworthy African countries. Another, Libya, is also eligible but does not currently need to borrow.
The 39 other countries can only borrow from the ADF, which provides interest-free loans repayable over 50 years.
Non-performing AfDB loans were cancelled and any undisbursed funds reallocated to creditworthy states.

Loan approvals and disbursements consequently declined in recent years, but the AfDB expects a sharp jump in the value of Bank loans approved in 1997 to 665 million units of account from 353.4 million in 1996.
AfDB President Omar Kabbaj told the audience that both concessional and non-concessional operations had been gathering momentum since the latter part of 1996.
"It should, therefore, be possible to make combined, annualised commitments of the order of $2.5 billion in the next two to three years," he said.
The AfDB expects to have cumulative loan loss provisions of 311 million units of account by the end of 1997, plus reserves of 1.06 billion.
AfDB officials said the combined reserves and provisions would be equivalent to nearly 20 percent of outstanding loans, against 17.2 percent at the end of 1996.
